# Final verification ledger

## Source and execution identity

The final native-default scientific qualification uses source commit `b71860fc4cc877298abf5dbb39a3716acc5f0cf4`. The complete performance campaigns use frozen candidate `a3acbf4dc9305c4d656399e9f98bc8360ddfa66f` and independent control `b157988355d2fabb6cbc62d56de18b203456897f`. Before default adoption, a source comparison confirmed that the production kernel/runtime implementation still matched the measured candidate. Subsequent numerical-header edits change three comments only; their old/new digests are recorded in `CompiledKernel/source-selection.json`. Runner selection, CMake defaults and documentation are separate from the measured numerical implementation.

The fresh native cache selected both Accelerate and `WV_RUNTIME_ENABLE_COMPACT_VARIABLE_POLICY=ON` without command-line overrides for either. It uses the pinned FFTW 3.3.11 provider. The [build receipt](default-qualification/build-receipt.json) records the exact source, compiler/cache, executable and provider identities. The host has 16 logical CPUs, 12 performance cores and 128 GiB physical memory. The actual variable policy uses twelve horizontal workers, eight pointwise workers and one internal FFTW worker.

## Completed checks

- Focused Release and ASan/UBSan checks passed for the three variable kernels and exact-group vertical operators. The retained-horizontal/spectral checks cover full-frequency derivatives, Nyquist rules, strides, input preservation, setup/worker/allocation failure cleanup and prepared allocation/lifetime guarantees. Runtime service construction and model/output tests passed. See the preceding [compact integration record](../issue-455-compact-integration/README.md) and [derivative-resource record](../issue-463-derivative-resources/README.md).
- Ten clean-path MATLAB transform methods passed, including reference/native and scalar/Accelerate configurations, compact/interleaved paths, odd/even nonsquare grids and exact/discontiguous Boussinesq groups. A clean-path recheck reproduced all five large saved MATLAB flux oracles bitwise. MATLAB was reset to the v4 source root to prevent class contamination from the separate v5 checkout.
- The bounded 45-run pointwise calibration selected eight workers. All 160 final direct-flux processes and all 120 final complete-model processes passed independent scientific checks. The complete-model campaigns include 237 full NetCDF graph comparisons. Source, worker, provider, fixture and harness postflight checks passed. Every required final time/memory gate passed; additional failed comparators remain recorded.
- Four focused tests passed in the fresh actual-default native build: `runner-variable-policy`, `standalone-runner`, `forward-integration-probe` and `barotropic-qg-native-fftw`. Earlier explicit-OFF portable runner/policy checks also passed. The final build invokes CTest with `--no-tests=error` and records exactly four executed tests.
- All six representative forward-integration cases passed with both reference and native FFTW providers: twelve executed provider cases. These retain nontrivial evolution, held amplitudes, all continuation directions, two output destinations, controlled stop/resume and dense-output comparisons. The 36 variable-family lifecycle reports explicitly confirm the expected native compact policy or reference scalar policy, including the worker counts and absence of an explicit FFT-thread request.
- Both current forward-integration qualification receipts were regenerated from the twelve fresh source-bound fragments. The prior top-level receipts and existing content-addressed artifacts were preserved. The source closure includes the runner policy implementation/header and both CMake inputs. No historical scientific result was rehashed or relabeled as a fresh run.
- The generated compatibility matrix changed exactly one source digest, for `TestPortableForwardIntegration.m`; its 1,794 rows and 74 witnesses are unchanged. The generated-assembly consistency test, eight forward-catalog tests and five compiled-source tests passed. The repository boundary/provenance check then passed.
- Code Analyzer found zero issues in the forward test, forward catalog test, validator and release-preparation helper. The compiled-source test has nine existing `PROP` findings about its local `runtimeSelection` variable; comparison with the measured baseline confirms the same nine messages and no new findings. Stable test code was not restyled to suppress them.

## Recorded interruptions and verification scope

The first Boussinesq timing campaign stopped in a warmup-progress summary before measured data existed. Its first scientific block passed; the interrupted run is retained and excluded. The corrected summary has four passing regression tests, and a fresh complete campaign supplies the decision.

The first forward postprocessing script incorrectly expected 18 logical CPUs, copied from a synthetic unit-test topology. All twelve scientific cases had already passed. Independent `sysctl` output and all 36 actual reports agree on 16 logical CPUs and 12 performance cores. The temporary assertion was corrected; only unfinished report collection, policy validation, catalog generation/tests and analysis resumed. The numerical campaign was not repeated. Original and corrected scripts, the failing postprocessing log and the explicit correction receipt are retained in the qualification archive.

Local MATLAB numerical/source verification used R2026a. Required hosted CI supplies its selected R2025b/R2026a, portable C++, sanitizer and packaging coverage before merge. No required check or branch protection is bypassed. Website generation is not repeated because website and inline MATLAB API-documentation inputs are unchanged. Performance timings ran serially without competing numerical or build jobs; evidence packaging and final functional verification began after timing finished.

Boussinesq 512, 512 complete-model execution and long-duration stability retain their documented qualification exclusions. Public MATLAB preview support and scientific feature-parity claims are unchanged. The independent MATLAB SQG tracer-construction bug remains tracked in #467.
